What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0052-0056 showed the wellhead at 19.2 °C with the air at 17.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored.

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

Maintenance Report — MNT-0052-007

Asset: WELL-0052 (SW-24 Well 052, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Dec 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 14 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0052-0062 on 2023-12-28 Report written: 31 Dec 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0052-0062 at 10:15 on 2023-12-28 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.5% of the pad area, estimated 3.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level; one crew member's monitor had not been bump-tested that day (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 209 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 167 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0052-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.58% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0052-010

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0052-0069 showed the wellhead at 13.5 °C with the air at 10.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 209 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 167 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0052-028 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.38% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
